newsitem.title: CHINA: GM's Hughes turns to China for satellite launches.
newsitem.headline: GM's Hughes turns to China for satellite launches.

text.p: China signed a long-term accord on Saturday to launch satellites for General Motors Corp's Hughes Space unit, the official Xinhua news agency said.
China would use its Long March series of rockets to launch at least five satellites with an option for five more for the U.S. auto giant's Hughes Space and Communications International subsidiary.
The launches would be made between the second half of 1998 and the end of 2006.
Xinhua said the agreement was signed between Hughes and China Great Wall Industry Corp, a state-run company that handles commercial space launch contracts with foreign companies.
The news agency called the agreement a sign of new progress in China's commercial space development programme.
China has been trying to repair damage to its reputation as a low-cost and reliable provider of commercial space services since a series of failures in 1995 and 1996.
It successfully launched a meteorological satellite into orbit on a Long March 3 rocket earlier this month.
In May, China put a defence satellite in orbit and successfully launched its Dongfanghong-3 communications satellite.
Chinese aerospace officials also have been hoping that the latest successful launches would enable them to hold down launch insurance rates which had risen sharply after the failures.
In August last year, a Hughes satellite aboard a Chinese Long March 3 rocket failed to reach proper orbit.

In China's most spectacular failure, a Long March 3B rocket carrying a satellite for the global organisation Intelsat veered off course and exploded in February last year. At least six people were killed and 57 injured on the ground.
